set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: When is intravenous antibiotic therapy used in Lyme disease?
opts: For some cutaneous manifestations, acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans and arthritis
Correct — ceftriaxone, cefotaxime or penicillin G are the agents named.
For every patient at the moment the erythema migrans lesion is first recognised
Early erythema migrans is treated orally.
For prophylaxis in anyone bitten by a tick in an endemic region of the country
Prophylaxis is not the described indication.
For patients who cannot tolerate doxycycline, in place of a macrolide antibiotic
Macrolides are the second-line oral option in that situation.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 80

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: How does a hobo spider bite present?
opts: An immediately painful sting with erythema, swelling and urticaria developing at the site
That describes a Hymenoptera sting.
A slowly advancing serpentine trail that progresses two to three centimetres each day
That describes cutaneous larva migrans.
A painless bite with induration and paraesthesia within thirty minutes, a large red area, and vesicles within thirty-six hours
Correct — eschar may follow, and systemic symptoms include headache, nausea and memory impairment.
A painful bite with sweating and piloerection within thirty minutes, then crampy abdominal pain and muscle spasms
That describes a black widow bite.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 64

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: What is characteristic of fire ant venom and behaviour?
opts: The venom is injected through hollow hairs, and contact occurs passively on brushing
That mechanism belongs to caterpillars.
The venom is cytotoxic, producing central necrosis with a surrounding blanched rim
That describes the brown recluse spider bite.
The venom induces mast cell degranulation, and the ants usually attack in groups
Correct — flushing, pruritus, hives, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea can follow.
The venom is a neurotoxin, and the insects sting only when their nest is disturbed
Alpha-latrotoxin is the neurotoxin of the black widow spider.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 42

set1.io: Objective c — Medical care strategies across infant, child, adolescent, adult and elderly populations
set1.q: In which patients might scabies excoriations be seen along the head and neck?
opts: Patients who have already been treated once
Prior treatment does not change the distribution.
Infants, the elderly and the immunocompromised
Correct — healthy adults have head and neck sparing.
Adolescents and young adults in shared housing
Crowding aids transmission but does not change the distribution.
Pregnant patients in their third trimester
Pregnancy affects treatment choice, not distribution.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 7

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: Which patients are at increased risk of complications from a black widow bite, and how is envenomation treated?
opts: The very old, the very young and those with cardiovascular disease; treat with calcium gluconate, narcotics, muscle relaxants and benzodiazepines
Correct, and tetanus vaccination status must be up to date.
Pregnant patients and children under eight years of age; treat with doxycycline given through a graded desensitisation protocol
That protocol belongs to Rocky Mountain spotted fever.
Immunosuppressed patients and the elderly; treat with ivermectin every two weeks for three doses
That regimen belongs to hyperkeratotic scabies.
Patients with a positive skin test; treat with subcutaneous epinephrine and desensitisation therapy
That belongs to Hymenoptera hypersensitivity.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 58

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: By which mechanisms do caterpillars produce skin disease?
opts: Burrowing into the stratum corneum where the organism deposits its eggs and faeces
That describes the scabies mite.
Mechanical irritation by pointed hairs, toxin injection through hollow hairs, and hypersensitivity to hairs
Correct — the aggregate of these effects is called lepidopterism.
Direct penetration of the skin by larvae that then migrate through the epidermal layer of the skin
That describes cutaneous larva migrans.
Injection of a neurotoxin through a modified ovipositor when the insect is threatened
That describes Hymenoptera stings.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 46

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: In whom is body louse infestation typically found, and how does it persist?
opts: Schoolchildren sharing hats and hair accessories, persisting through repeated close head contact
That describes head lice.
Sexually active adults across all social levels, often with a concurrent sexually transmitted infection
That describes pubic lice.
Long-term care residents who are elderly and immunosuppressed, persisting through staff carriage
That describes facility-associated scabies.
Homeless people, refugees, war victims and those in crowded conditions, persisting via unwashed clothing
Correct — transmission is through contaminated clothing and bedding.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 24

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: Which three lice cause pediculosis, and which body regions do they affect?
opts: Phthirus pubis on the scalp, Pediculus humanus capitis on pubic skin, and Cimex pilosellus on the trunk
None of those pairings is correct.
Pediculus humanus capitis on the scalp, Pediculus humanus humanus on the trunk, Phthirus pubis on pubic skin
Correct. The body louse is about 30% larger than the head louse.
Pediculus humanus capitis on the trunk, Pediculus humanus humanus on the scalp, Phthirus pubis on the eyelashes
The first two are the wrong way round.
Sarcoptes scabiei on the scalp, Cimex lectularius on the trunk, and Phthirus pubis on pubic skin
The first two organisms are the scabies mite and the bedbug.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 23

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: What is hookworm folliculitis?
opts: Pustules on an erythematous base each pierced by a single central hair shaft
That is ordinary bacterial folliculitis.
Indurated crusted nodules on the trunk of an infant with heavy infestation
Those nodules occur in infantile scabies.
Follicular papules and pustules confined to one location, usually the buttock
Correct — it may need repeated courses of treatment.
Follicular pustules over the trunk and buttocks after hot tub exposure
That is Pseudomonas folliculitis from the previous lecture.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 51

set1.io: Objective c — Medical care strategies across infant, child, adolescent, adult and elderly populations
set1.q: Which age group is most affected by head lice, and how is it usually transmitted?
opts: Homeless adults, primarily by contaminated clothing that cannot be washed or changed
That describes body lice.
Infants under one year, primarily by contact with the bedding of an infested carer
Head lice predominate in the three to twelve year age band.
Children between three and twelve years, primarily by direct head-to-head contact
Correct. Indirect spread through combs, brushes, bedding and headgear is less common.
Adults over forty years, primarily by sexual contact and shared towels or bedding
That describes pubic lice.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 24

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: Which organism causes Lyme disease, and how is it maintained in the environment?
opts: Borrelia burgdorferi, a spirochete, maintained by transstadial passage through tick life stages with birds and deer as dispersal animals
Correct — it occurs across the northern hemisphere in North America, Europe and Asia.
Rickettsia rickettsii, a bacterium, maintained in dog ticks, wood ticks and rodents across the southeastern and south central states
That organism causes Rocky Mountain spotted fever.
Sarcoptes scabiei, maintained by close contact between humans in crowded living conditions
That organism causes scabies.
A parasitic flatworm, maintained in snails and waterfowl in fresh water and released as cercariae
That organism causes cercarial dermatitis.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 68

set1.io: Objective b — Differentiate primary from secondary skin lesions
set1.q: Once a reaction pattern has been recognised, how is the differential narrowed further?
opts: By the duration of the eruption, the patient's age, and whether treatment has been tried
Those are useful clinically but are not the characteristics named here.
By culture and sensitivity of the lesion together with a complete blood count
Laboratory testing is not what refines the morphological differential.
By whether the patient reports pruritus and whether there is regional lymphadenopathy
Symptoms and nodes are helpful but are not the named characteristics.
By colour, shape, configuration of lesions relative to one another, and distribution on the body
Correct. Those characteristics tune the differential the reaction pattern generated.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 3

set1.io: Objective c — Medical care strategies across infant, child, adolescent, adult and elderly populations
set1.q: How is Rocky Mountain spotted fever treated, including in pregnancy and young children?
opts: Intravenous ceftriaxone for all patients, with oral therapy reserved for prophylaxis
That is not the described regimen.
Doxycycline for adults, pregnant patients and children, with desensitisation where it is contraindicated
Correct — 100 mg twice daily for adults and 2.2 mg per kilogram twice daily for children, for 5 to 10 days.
Amoxicillin for children and pregnant patients, with doxycycline reserved for adults only
That substitution belongs to Lyme disease rather than this one.
Azithromycin for all patients, since doxycycline is contraindicated below eight years of age
Desensitisation allows doxycycline to be used even in those groups.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 86

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: Which distribution is typical of scabies in a healthy adult?
opts: Back, neck, shoulders and waist as linear excoriations, with post-inflammatory pigmentation
That is the distribution of body lice.
Interdigital webs, sides of fingers, volar wrists, elbows, axillae and genitalia, sparing head and neck
Correct. The areolae are also involved in women.
Scalp and hairline first, then spreading down the neck and onto the upper back over weeks
Head and neck are spared in healthy adults.
Ankles and wrists first, then spreading centripetally to involve the palms and the soles
That is the spread of the Rocky Mountain spotted fever rash.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 7

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: What are maculae caeruleae and which infestation produces them?
opts: Linear excoriations on the back, neck, shoulders and waist with post-inflammatory pigmentation, in body lice
Those are the signs of body lice rather than this finding.
Two millimetre erythematous macules or papules with scaling and excoriation, seen in head lice
Those are the lesions of head lice.
A central violaceous area ringed by blanched skin and then by asymmetric erythema, in spider bites
That is the red, white and blue sign of the brown recluse.
Slate-grey to bluish irregular macules about 1 cm across representing haemorrhage, seen in pubic lice
Correct, alongside papular urticaria at the feeding sites, commonly periumbilical.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 26

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: How is hyperkeratotic scabies in an immunosuppressed patient treated?
opts: Topical permethrin applied overnight on a single occasion with no repeat application at all
That is inadequate even for ordinary scabies, which needs a second application.
Oral albendazole 400 mg daily for three days with no topical therapy given alongside it
That is the treatment of cutaneous larva migrans.
Oral doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for ten to fourteen days as monotherapy
That regimen belongs to tick-borne illness.
Ivermectin every two weeks for two to three doses, with topical permethrin every three days to weekly
Correct — that combination is used when individual therapy fails.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 19

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: Which organism causes scabies and how is it usually transmitted?
opts: Pediculus humanus capitis, by direct head-to-head contact between two individuals
That organism and route belong to head lice.
Cimex lectularius, by spread in the clothing and baggage of travellers and visitors
That organism and route belong to bedbugs.
Borrelia burgdorferi, by the blood meal of a tick that has fed on a reservoir animal
That organism and route belong to Lyme disease.
Sarcoptes scabiei variety hominis, by close physical contact for fifteen to twenty minutes
Correct. It may also be acquired from the bedding or underclothing of an infested person.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 5

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: How should a honeybee sting be removed and why?
opts: Apply ice for twenty minutes first, then remove it once the swelling has settled
Delay allows more venom to be pumped in.
Scrape it off with a card edge or dull knife held parallel to the skin, as fast as possible
Correct — the barbed ovipositor stays impaled and continues to pump venom.
Grasp it with fine forceps and pull it straight out with steady traction on the shaft
Scraping parallel to the surface is the described technique.
Leave it in place, since removing it releases the remaining venom into the tissue
It should be removed as fast as possible.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 42

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: What is the hallmark sign of a brown recluse bite?
opts: The bull's eye sign — a lesion over 5 cm with central clearing and a darker punctate centre
That is erythema migrans in Lyme disease.
The train-track sign — two parallel rows of purpura at the site of contact with the skin
That is the asp or puss caterpillar sting.
The red, white and blue sign — a central violaceous area, a blanched rim, then large asymmetric erythema
Correct. Reactions range from mild and local to severe ulcerative necrosis.
The delta-wing jet sign — a dense dark head with the body, eggs and burrow trailing behind it
That is a dermoscopic sign in scabies.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 60

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: Which physical methods are described for head lice, and what is their limitation?
opts: Weekly application of an occlusive agent such as mayonnaise or mineral oil to smother the live lice and eggs
Those alternatives may not be lethal to lice.
Head shaving, or combing nits out after two minutes of hair moisturiser every few days; effective but slow and painful
Correct — they need adjuvant therapy alongside them.
Head shaving alone, which is completely curative and requires no further treatment at all
Physical methods need adjuvant therapy.
Daily hot air drying of the scalp, which kills both the live lice and the attached eggs
Hair is dried after combing rather than used as the treatment itself.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 30

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: Which specific physical measure is used in caterpillar exposure?
opts: Stripping the hairs off the skin with adhesive tape
Correct, alongside symptomatic therapy and antivenom for certain categories.
Scraping the site with a card edge held parallel to the skin
That is the technique for removing a honeybee stinger.
Applying blue or black ink and looking for a zigzag line
That is the burrow ink test for scabies.
Combing the area after applying a hair moisturiser for two minutes
That is a physical method used for head lice.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 48

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: What causes cercarial dermatitis, also called swimmer's itch?
opts: Penetration of the stratum corneum by a mite that tunnels through it as it moves
That describes scabies.
Penetration of the skin by the cercarial larval form of certain parasitic flatworms
Correct — the cercaria passes from an intermediate host such as a snail to another host.
Penetration of the skin by the larva of an animal hookworm from contaminated soil
That describes cutaneous larva migrans.
Penetration of the skin by an adult female flea that then lays her eggs within it
That describes tungiasis.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 88

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: Describe the classic lesion of cutaneous larva migrans.
opts: A large expanding round lesion over 5 cm with central clearing at the site of a bite
That is erythema migrans in Lyme disease.
Erythematous papules in linear streaks after brushing against a caterpillar's hairs
That is caterpillar dermatitis.
An erythematous, raised, vesicular, linear or serpentine trail advancing 2 to 3 cm each day
Correct — intensely pruritic and painful, lasting two to eight weeks, with rare systemic symptoms.
A thin thread-like linear or J-shaped tunnel 1 to 10 mm long in the interdigital webs
That is the scabies burrow.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 51

set1.io: Objective b — Differentiate primary from secondary skin lesions
set1.q: How do primary and secondary skin lesions differ in the depth they affect?
opts: Primary lesions affect the epidermis and superficial dermis; secondary lesions infiltrate the dermis or subcutaneous tissue
Correct. Their combination determines the diagnostic category, also called the reaction pattern.
Primary lesions infiltrate the dermis and subcutaneous tissue; secondary lesions affect only the superficial epidermis
That reverses the two definitions.
Primary lesions arise from infection while secondary lesions arise from an immune reaction to that infection
The distinction is anatomical rather than causal.
Primary lesions appear first in time while secondary lesions appear only after treatment has been started
The distinction is not about the order in which they appear.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 3

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: What draws bedbugs out to feed, and where do they hide during the day?
opts: Warmth and carbon dioxide draw them out; they hide in cracks and crevices of headboards and picture frames
Correct — they also hide behind loose wallpaper and in other dark places.
Light and movement draw them out; they hide in the seams of clothing worn close to the skin
Clothing seams are where body lice and their nits are found.
Perspiration and body odour draw them out; they burrow into the stratum corneum of the skin
Burrowing into the stratum corneum describes the scabies mite.
Blood on the skin surface draws them out; they live permanently attached to the hair shaft
Attachment to the hair shaft describes lice and their nits.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 32

set1.io: Objective c — Medical care strategies across infant, child, adolescent, adult and elderly populations
set1.q: Why is facility-associated scabies a particular concern?
opts: Residents are homeless or displaced, in whom infestation persists through unwashed clothing
That describes body lice.
Residents travel frequently, carrying the organism between facilities in luggage and bedding
That describes bedbug spread.
Residents are elderly and immunosuppressed, and a hospital epidemic can follow their admission
Correct, and it is difficult to eradicate once healthcare workers are infested.
Residents are children under twelve, in whom the infestation spreads through shared headgear
That describes head lice in schoolchildren.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 5

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: How often do bedbugs need a blood meal, and how long can they survive without one?
opts: Every one to two days, and they die within a week without one
That underestimates both the interval and the survival.
Once a month, and they can survive for up to three months
That is not the interval the lecture gives.
Twice daily, and they cannot survive more than forty-eight hours
That is far more frequent than described.
Every five to ten days, but they can survive for up to a year
Correct, which is why an unoccupied room does not clear an infestation.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 32

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: What is the prognosis and treatment of a hobo spider bite?
opts: Wounds require surgical reconstruction and healing takes months; treatment is operative
That is the course of a severe brown recluse bite.
Wounds resolve within hours; treatment is calcium gluconate with muscle relaxants
That is envenomation treatment for a black widow bite.
Wounds resolve within days; treatment is a ten-day course of oral doxycycline
Antibiotics have no role in this envenomation.
Wounds heal within several weeks and headaches may last a week; treatment is supportive
Correct — death from severe systemic effects, including aplastic anaemia, is rare.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 65

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: Which diseases do rat fleas and cat fleas transmit?
opts: Rat fleas transmit bubonic plague; cat fleas are a vector for bubonic plague and endemic typhus
Correct — both belong to the family Pulicidae.
Rat fleas transmit Lyme disease; cat fleas are a vector for Rocky Mountain spotted fever
Those are both tick-borne rather than flea-borne.
Rat fleas transmit tungiasis; cat fleas are a vector for cutaneous larva migrans
Tungiasis is caused by a different flea family and larva migrans by hookworms.
Rat fleas transmit endemic typhus only; cat fleas transmit no human disease at all
Cat fleas are a vector for two named diseases.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 37

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: When is serological testing for Lyme disease most useful?
opts: In patients who do not live in an endemic region and present with signs possibly consistent with it
Correct — a patient with erythema migrans is diagnosed and treated clinically.
In every patient who reports a tick bite, regardless of whether any rash has developed
Testing is not indicated for every tick bite.
In patients with erythema migrans, in whom the result determines whether to treat
Those patients are diagnosed and treated on clinical grounds.
In patients from endemic regions, in whom a negative result excludes the diagnosis
Testing is described as most helpful outside endemic regions.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 77

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set2.q: How does a black widow spider bite present within the first thirty minutes?
opts: A painless bite with induration and paraesthesia at the site, then a large area of erythema around it
That describes the hobo spider bite.
A central violaceous area ringed by blanched skin and then a large asymmetric red area
That is the red, white and blue sign of the brown recluse.
Immediate burning and pain with local erythema, swelling and urticaria at the site
That is the typical Hymenoptera sting reaction.
Localised erythema, piloerection and sweating around the bite, then crampy abdominal pain and muscle spasm
Correct — headache, paraesthesia, nausea, vomiting, hypertension and seizures may follow.
set2.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 57

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set2.q: What is the time course of a severe brown recluse bite?
opts: Necrosis at six weeks, eschar at eight weeks, with no systemic symptoms at any stage
That is far slower than the described course.
Vesicle formation in the first thirty-six hours, then healing over several weeks
That is the course of a hobo spider bite.
Necrosis at two to three days, eschar between days five and seven, then deep ulcers; systemic symptoms at one to two days
Correct — nausea, vomiting, headache, fever and chills make up the systemic picture.
Necrosis within thirty minutes, eschar within six hours, then deep ulcers by the end of the first day; systemic symptoms at once
That is far faster than the described course.
set2.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 61

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set2.q: What is the classic manifestation of stage 3, late persistent Lyme disease?
opts: Cranial nerve palsies, meningitis and radiculopathies developing over days to weeks
Those belong to stage 2, early disseminated disease.
A single expanding erythematous lesion with central clearing at the site of the bite
That is the stage 1 lesion.
A blanching rash spreading centripetally from the ankles and wrists to the trunk
That is Rocky Mountain spotted fever.
Monoarticular or oligoarticular arthritis affecting the knee or weight-bearing joints
Correct — subacute encephalopathy and acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans also occur.
set2.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 75

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set2.q: Which complications of scabies are named, and how are the persistent papules treated?
opts: Necrotic ulceration requiring surgical reconstruction once the wound has become stable
That belongs to brown recluse spider bites.
Staphylococcal superinfection, post-scabietic papules treated with potent or intralesional steroid, and psychological effects
Correct — intralesional triamcinolone acetonide is given at 2.5 to 5 mg per millilitre.
Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, treated with supportive care while the kidney function recovers on its own
That complication follows impetigo in the previous lecture.
Acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans, treated with intravenous ceftriaxone over several weeks
That complication belongs to late Lyme disease.
set2.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 21

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set2.q: What does light microscopy with mineral oil show in cutaneous larva migrans?
opts: Live and dead larvae, particularly in patients with folliculitis
Correct — histology shows larvae with an eosinophilic infiltrate.
Mites, ova and faecal pellets scraped from an unexcoriated burrow
That is what the scabies scraping shows.
Ovoid eggs visible within the lesion when viewed on dermoscopy
That describes the diagnosis of tungiasis.
Nits attached at the base of hairs plucked from the affected area
That describes the confirmation of pubic lice.
set2.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 53

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set2.q: Where is the hobo spider found and what is it often mistaken for?
opts: The Great Lakes region, where it is mistaken for a harmless house spider entirely
That region is associated with cercarial dermatitis.
The Pacific Northwest, where it is the predominant cause of necrotic arachnidism and is mistaken for the brown recluse
Correct — it is brown with a grey herringbone pattern and bites from July to September.
The American Midwest and Southeast, where it is the predominant necrotic spider and is mistaken for the tarantula
That geography belongs to the brown recluse.
All but the most northern states, where it is mistaken for the black widow spider
That geography belongs to the black widow.
set2.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 63

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set2.q: What is the position on prophylactic antibiotics after a tick bite in a Rocky Mountain spotted fever area?
opts: A single dose of doxycycline is recommended for every tick bite
Prophylaxis is specifically not recommended.
